overview: This table holds the story words players see, including chapter names, mission titles, explanations, short story names, and credits text.
description: Localized story-facing UI strings rather than script dialogue: nine CHAP_* chapter titles, 115 STMSN_* mission/demo titles plus 115 matching *_EXPLANATION blurbs, 45 STR_STDM_SS_* short-story titles, and three STR_DEMO_LABEL_* credits labels. StoryChapter, StoryDemo, ShortStory, and short-story Item rows point at these ids; spoken story dialogue is carried by StoryDemoTextDataTable/ShortStoryDemoTextDataTable.

ID.simple: The name that connects this line of text to its chapter, mission, short story, or item.
ID.technical: FName ID in FGameDataTableRow_GameText (row +0x0). UDataTable::FindRow uses the row name, not a scan of the ID column, and all 11 exports have ID equal to their row name. Non-SYS_ ids are searched in AGameTextManager::TextDataTables, a 14-table array rebuilt on culture load with StoryTextDataTable_<Language> as the seventh entry (array index 6); FindTextRow returns the first matching row. No StoryText key overlaps a row of the other 13 GameText tables in the exports. Callers reach this table through chapter/mission/short-story/item text-id fields, widget SetTextIdOnly/SetTextRequest, GetText/GetGameText/GetGameTextById, and nested FGameTextRequestParameters; HasText tests row existence while HasGameTextContent additionally requires nonempty Text. NAME_None or an invalid text request clears text-block content instead of matching a row.

Text.simple: The player sees this wording as a chapter or mission title, a story explanation, or a credits label. Modders change it to edit what appears in the chosen language.
Text.technical: FString Text at row +0x10. A missing row gives an empty string, and HasGameTextContent is false for an empty value. GetGameText copies Text and passes it through the generic FormatText, which substitutes <GLO=...> tags from GlossaryParameters and <DYN=...> tags from request parameters; no GLO/DYN tags occur in any of the 11 StoryText exports, though callers do pass MISSION_NAME as a nested text-id parameter into surrounding SYS_DIALOG_MESSAGE_0301 messages. One En explanation row contains a literal newline; text blocks with bForceOneLine set apply GameText_JoinLines (CRLF/LF removed for Ja/Zh_Hant/Zh_Hans, replaced with a space otherwise). Every export has 287 unique keys with nonempty Text.

notes: Exports and loading: the 11 language variants (De, En, Es, Es_LA, Fr, It, Ja, Ko, Pt, Zh_Hans, Zh_Hant) each contain the same 287 keys in the same order and all Text values are nonempty: 9 CHAP_*, 115 STMSN_* titles, 115 matching STMSN_*_EXPLANATION rows, 45 STR_STDM_SS_*, and 3 STR_DEMO_LABEL_*. The row struct is /Script/Abrams.GameDataTableRow_GameText with only ID and Text. Config/DefaultGame.ini:35-45 assigns the language suffixes to chunks 1-11.

Lookup and precedence: StartLanguageLoading builds <Base>_<Language> asset names, and Tick installs only the selected language variant. The 14-table TextDataTables order is fixed and lookup stops at the first row match; no StoryText id collides with another GameText table in any exported language. FindTextIdsContaining instead collects matching IDs from all 14 tables by applying Id.Contains(Key). GameScript_GetStoryTextId derives STDM_* keys, and the observed matching dialogue resides in StoryDemoTextDataTable/ShortStoryDemoTextDataTable; no script key or exported source row demonstrates that this scan obtains dialogue from StoryTextDataTable. Do not infer dialogue use merely from the unguarded scan.

Verified data relationships: StoryChapter.Id_StoryChapterTitle -> CHAP_*; StoryDemo.Id_StoryMissionTitle -> STMSN_* title and StoryDemo.Id_StoryMissionDetail -> the paired *_EXPLANATION row; ShortStory.Id_StoryText_Title -> STR_STDM_SS_*; and all 45 ITM_SHORT_STORY_* rows in ItemDataTable use Id_ItemText with the same STR_STDM_SS_* id, which GameItem_GetNameTextCore leaves unchanged for ItemType ShortStory so item-name widgets resolve the StoryText row. All 9 chapter titles, 115 mission titles, 115 explanation ids, and 45 short-story title pointers resolve in the En export. The 3 STR_DEMO_LABEL_* rows have no C++ caller or exported table field reference found.

Indirect consumers trace through widget text blocks and nested requests: chapter/dlc chapter select, mission select and its explanation panel, character-select mission info, story-demo title cards, archive movie cards, character-correlation mission and short-story buttons, item descriptions, shop unlock requests, and system dialog MISSION_NAME parameters. Locked archive items and locked/new short-story entries substitute SYS_* labels instead of reading a StoryText row. ShowTitle additionally requires a matching demo, a chapter containing it, and a loaded thumbnail before setting the title ids.

Values and sentinels: this table has no numeric or unit fields, and its constructor supplies only default FName/FString values. ChapterIndex and MissionIndex are integer parameters on separate SYS_* labels in the demo-title widgets, not fields or units of StoryText rows. Passing EApplicationLanguage::Invalid to SetButtonTextId selects the current-language text-block path; it is not a missing-row sentinel. Retail Blueprint assets were not inspected, so which specific widget instances have bForceOneLine enabled and the final on-screen presentation are not independently verified.

Reconstruction caveat: FindTextRow/0x14af290 is behaviour-certified in BEHAV NA15 and Tick/0x14c96f0 in BEHAV BG03; FindTextIdsContaining/0x14b0100 is a fragmented match with a HOLD verdict and an unresolved call identity. These establish reconstructed behaviour, not byte-identical whole-function proofs. No exhaustive retail Blueprint-consumer claim is made.

usages.detail: Builds the language-suffixed table name and installs StoryTextDataTable_<Language> as the seventh of 14 shared GameText tables; first matching row wins for non-SYS_ ids.
FindTextIdsContaining scans IDs from all 14 GameText tables; observed script-derived STDM_* keys match StoryDemoText/ShortStoryDemoText, not these CHAP_/STMSN_/STR_ rows.
Sets the chapter-select title from StoryChapter.Id_StoryChapterTitle; the DLC variant does the same at GameStoryDlcChapterSelectWidget.cpp:121.
Sets the mission-select chapter title from Id_StoryChapterTitle. The detail panel at lines 601-602 sets the mission title from Id_StoryMissionTitle and the explanation from Id_StoryMissionDetail.

ShowTitle requires a script-matched demo, a chapter containing it, and a thumbnail, then passes chapter and mission title ids to GameStoryDemoWidget::SetupTitle, which applies them at GameStoryDemoWidget.cpp:223.
Unlocked archive movie items show StoryDemo.Id_StoryMissionTitle; locked items use a SYS_* placeholder label instead.
Unlocked short-story buttons show ShortStory.Id_StoryText_Title; locked/new entries use a SYS_* placeholder instead.
Shows StoryDemo.Id_StoryMissionTitle on character-correlation mission list buttons when the data row is found.
Adds Id_StoryChapterTitle as a nested MISSION_NAME text-id parameter to SYS_DIALOG_MESSAGE_0301; line 149 does the same with Id_StoryMissionTitle for mission lists.

Shop lineup unlock text resolves chapter names through Id_StoryChapterTitle; mission names use Id_StoryMissionTitle at lines 1361 and 1538, and line 1775 supplies it as MISSION_NAME to ITM_UNLOCK_MESSAGE_4020.
GameItem_GetNameTextCore passes ItemDataTable.Id_ItemText through unchanged for ShortStory items, so the 45 ITM_SHORT_STORY_* rows resolve their STR_STDM_SS_* titles from this table.
SetTextIdOnly builds the text request, caches the id for language refreshes, and clears content for invalid requests; SetText at line 206 applies conditional GameText_JoinLines formatting.
